category_rationale: maps → vector lane, as a SCHEMATIC transit-line map (a Liniennetzplan), not geography. The piece is exactly the maps signature set: a route drawn on with stroke-dashoffset, a traveller ("flyer") moving along it, stops lit in sequence (pin-rollout) and a callout card pinned to the current stop (the module's callout-card overlay). The maps module's hard rules are the ones this hero must obey: restraint (no glows / blobs / particles; colour carries meaning — türkis = built, pale = Im Bau, sun = free), legibility (labels offset from shapes, callouts clamped to the safe area, never on another label) and determinism (no tl.call, pre-hold hidden states). kinetic-type was the runner-up — the sentences are the payoff — but its caption-* blocks animate captions, and here the text only rides in on a card; its "no bounce on text" restraint is carried over. No D3 / TopoJSON / basemap is used.
style: Die Linie v4 "Türkis": a flat, Swiss-transit-diagram hero on white. One türkis line, ring stations, a little tram and a white speech card — editorial, calm, confident; motion is the only flourish. Restraint: no decoration, no particles, no gradient sweeps, no glow.
palette_rules: Define every colour once as a CSS custom property on the root (--bg, --line, --line-deep, --edge, --wash, --pale, --rule, --ink, --muted, --sun); no inline hex in markup.
Sun #FBBF24 appears ONLY as the "Free" tag fill on A1.1. Nothing else is yellow.
Built (A1.1–A2.2): türkis rings, solid track, ink codes. Im Bau (B1.1–B2.2): pale #BFEAE3 dashed rings, dashed pale track, muted #3F5A55 codes.
No gradients, no glows, no particles, no sweeps, no decorative shapes. The hairline bed is structure, not decoration (design-token rule 3: hairlines, not resting shadows).

font_notes: Aliased family names ('Archivo DM', 'Nunito Sans DM') on purpose: the compiler bundles / Google-fetches fonts BY NAME, and a unique alias guarantees the owner's local files are what renders. The in-file @font-face also satisfies lint font_family_without_font_face.
Build the timeline after document.fonts.ready (supported by hyperframes-core) because bubble widths and clamps are measured from the laid-out text.
Relative url() paths assume the composition HTML sits at the project root next to assets/; adjust the prefix (../assets/…) if it lives in compositions/.
poster_note: All eight stations lit (4 türkis discs + 4 pale discs), the train parked at B2.2, the B2.2 bubble ("Einerseits ist es teuer, / andererseits lohnt es sich." + B2.2 and Im Bau chips) fully in, and the A1.1 Free tag visible. Export the still with `npx hyperframes snapshot --at 12.6` for the reduced-motion poster.

motion_rules: ONE paused GSAP timeline on window.__timelines["<composition-id>"]; tl.seek(0); deterministic; no tl.call, no proxies/onUpdate (dash and clip values are tweened directly so a suppressed seek still renders them).
Only transform (x, y, scale), opacity, stroke-dashoffset and clip-path are tweened. No filter, no colour tweens, no width/height.
Entrances: power2.out / power3.out. Train travel: power2.inOut. Exits: power2.in. No back / elastic / bounce anywhere.

Every later-entering element uses fromTo with an explicit hidden start (immediateRender) so frames before its entrance are correct under seek in both directions. Never tween a .clip itself — animate children inside one full-duration clip.
Author each station as <g transform="translate(x y)"> holding an inner <g> centred on 0,0 that GSAP scales — avoids SVG transform-origin / fill-box pitfalls (svg-icon-enrichment note).
Exactly ONE bubble visible at any time: bubble k is out by stop_window_end+0.20 and bubble k+1 starts at its stop+0.28 — a 0.08 s gap, never an overlap.

shot_brief: A white card; a faint hairline marks the route. In the first second the line draws itself across the lower half in türkis — solid through the four built stops, then pale and dashed through the four that are Im Bau — and each station ring pops in as the front passes it, its code beneath it and a small sun-yellow "Free" tag under A1.1. A little türkis tram pulls in at A1.1 and from then on glides stop to stop (left to right), braking with a tiny settle; as it parks, the station fills and a white speech card lifts in above it with that level's German sentence — growing from "Guten Tag! Ich heiße Ana." to "Einerseits ist es teuer, andererseits lohnt es sich." — so the viewer watches the promise of the line come true. The one pattern-interrupt: at the B-levels the track turns dashed and pale and every card gains an "Im Bau" chip, yet the tram keeps going. After B2.2 (the poster frame, every station lit) the card lifts away, the tram rolls off the right edge, the line clears behind it and the frame returns to the bare hairline it started from — a 14-second loop with no seam. Single dominant motif: THE LINE.
